claimedEvidence.claim:
Scan complete. I read patches/review-candidate.patch (a one-line change to SESSION_TTL_SECONDS in service.py, 24h -> 30min), service.py, tests/test_service.py, README.md, jobs/README.md, requirements.txt, CHANGELOG-vendored.md, and the sibling patches/main-moved.patch, and verified behavior empirically by applying the patch to a scratch copy in /tmp (the repo itself was never modified) and running the test suite there: the patch applies cleanly but 1 of 6 tests fails (test_session_ttl_is_24h, AssertionError: 1800 != 86400). The removed code comment, the test's own "Contract decision 2024-06" note, and the sibling patch (which keeps the 24h default and adds an env override instead) all indicate the constant is deliberately pinned. The patch also does not deliver its stated goal: the README documents 30 minutes of inactivity, but session_expired() keys off created_at, which is never refreshed, so the change is a shorter creation-age limit, not an inactivity window. Verdict: not safe to merge as-is. Pre-existing issues (raw markdown HTML persisted and returned, non-atomic store writes, millisecond session-id collisions) are reported separately and not attributed to this diff.
